title: TG Therapeutics Research Report
name: TG Therapeutics
tagline: TG Therapeutics turned a collapsed cancer program into a roughly $1B multiple sclerosis business. Its drug Briumvi is a one-hour infusion given twice a year. The stock fell about 90% in 2022 and has since risen more than fifteen-fold.

chapters.title: The founding story
chapters.lede: TG Therapeutics was built around one antibody, ublituximab, a re-engineered anti-CD20 drug licensed in 2012. Chairman and CEO Michael Weiss first bet on blood cancers. When that program collapsed in 2022, the company was left with its multiple sclerosis trials, and those became the entire business.

items: Chairman and CEO. He steered the company through the 2022 cancer withdrawal and into a successful MS launch.
The molecule behind everything. It is an anti-CD20 antibody engineered to kill B cells efficiently, which allows a short one-hour infusion.
Ex-US rights to Briumvi are licensed to a European partner. TG keeps the US market, where most of the revenue is.
TG licenses the anti-CD20 antibody that would become Briumvi and builds the company around it.
TG pairs ublituximab with umbralisib, an oral PI3K-delta inhibitor, for chronic lymphocytic leukemia and lymphoma. It also runs the ULTIMATE Phase 3 trials in MS.
Umbralisib (Ukoniq) gets FDA accelerated approval for two lymphomas, and the stock nears $50.
Overall-survival concerns in the UNITY-CLL trial lead TG to withdraw its cancer applications and pull Ukoniq from the market. The FDA also delays the MS decision.
The stock falls about 90% from its peak, leaving MS as the only program.
The FDA approves Briumvi (ublituximab) for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.
Briumvi goes up against Roche's Ocrevus and Novartis's Kesimpta and wins share with its one-hour infusion. Ex-US rights are partnered.
Sales compound, and subcutaneous Briumvi enters Phase 3.
Q3 Briumvi US sales rise 52%. Global 2026 guidance goes up to about $1B, and TG buys back $100M of stock.

chapters.title: Early challenges
chapters.lede: Few biotechs survive having their lead cancer drug withdrawn and then out-launch two of the world's biggest drug makers. Tap a card to see how TG got through each problem.

items: Ukoniq was withdrawn in 2022 after a possible increase in the risk of death, and the FDA tightened scrutiny of the whole PI3K drug class.
TG voluntarily withdrew all its cancer applications, cut costs and put everything behind the MS program.
The FDA pushed back Briumvi's MS decision just as the cancer program fell apart.
Briumvi was approved in December 2022. The ULTIMATE trials, run against an active comparator, made the data hard to dispute.
Roche's Ocrevus and Novartis's Kesimpta already dominated anti-CD20 MS treatment.
TG competed on convenience, with a one-hour infusion every six months after the first doses, and with price and service for infusion centers.
With no approved product in mid-2022, the company had to fund a launch while its market value was at its lowest.
Fast Briumvi uptake turned TG profitable. It now buys back stock, about $100M in Q3 2026 alone.
Kesimpta is a monthly self-injection and Roche has a subcutaneous Ocrevus. Briumvi is only infused.
A subcutaneous Briumvi Phase 3 reads out at the end of 2026 or early 2027. TG models quarterly dosing and is targeting a 2028 launch.
Almost all revenue comes from Briumvi in one country.
TG is running Phase 2 programs in myasthenia gravis and treatment-resistant schizophrenia, plus azer-cel, a cell therapy for autoimmune disease.

chapters.title: Growth
chapters.lede: Briumvi took less than four years to go from launch to about $900M of US sales. Growth is still above 50% but is slowing as the base gets larger.

blocks.html: Watch-out: growth fell from 64% to 52% in one quarter. The market is now valuing TG on how long Briumvi can keep taking share, and on whether a subcutaneous version can defend it once Ocrevus faces biosimilars later this decade.

chapters.title: Stock trajectory
chapters.lede: Few stocks have had a round trip like this. TG rose to about $48 on the Ukoniq approval, fell to about $4 when the cancer program collapsed, and climbed more than fifteen-fold on Briumvi. Hover over the line, switch to the S&P 500 comparison, or click an event.

events: Accelerated approval in two lymphomas. The stock was near its high.
Overall-survival concerns: TG withdraws its applications and Ukoniq.
About $4, down roughly 90% from the peak.
The FDA approves it for relapsing MS, and the turnaround begins.
Initial 2026 guidance trailed consensus despite projected growth of about 54%, and the stock fell into the $20s.
Shares rose about 6% on the raised guidance.

chapters.title: The MS market & pipeline
chapters.lede: Anti-CD20 antibodies, which deplete the B cells that drive MS attacks, have become the leading high-efficacy treatment for relapsing MS. Three drugs compete, and convenience is now the main battleground.

items.title: Briumvi (TG)
items.sub: infusion, twice a year after the first doses
items.text: TG's MS drug has the shortest infusion in the class. It is popular with infusion centers and patients who don't want monthly shots.

items.title: Ocrevus (Roche)
items.text: The category's original blockbuster, with an infused version and a subcutaneous version.
items.more: Biosimilar competition to Ocrevus later in the decade could pressure prices across the class.

items.title: Kesimpta (Novartis)
items.text: Its home self-injection gives Novartis a format advantage that TG doesn't yet have.

items.title: Subcutaneous Briumvi
items.text: This is TG's answer to the format gap. Pharmacokinetic modeling supports quarterly dosing, and the launch target is 2028.

items.title: Beyond MS
items.text: These are Phase 2 work in generalized myasthenia gravis and treatment-resistant schizophrenia, plus azer-cel, a cell therapy for autoimmune disease.
items.more: Kyverna's KYV-101 is an emerging rival to azer-cel in MS, though its early data come from only a handful of patients.

chapters.title: What the company prizes
chapters.lede: TG's strategy since 2022 has been narrow: win in B-cell therapy for MS, then use the cash it generates for new formats, new indications and buybacks. Tap a priority to see how it shows up in practice.

blocks.label: Priority
items: Compete on patient and clinic time, not just efficacy.
Briumvi's one-hour infusion, and a subcutaneous version modeled for quarterly dosing.
Put everything behind the program that works.
After 2022 TG dropped oncology entirely and concentrated on MS.
Win infusion centers and neurologists one at a time.
US sales went from about $89M in 2023 to a guided $915–920M in 2026.
Use what it knows about B cells in other immune diseases.
Phase 2 programs in myasthenia gravis and schizophrenia, and azer-cel.
Return cash once the business is self-funding.
It bought back about $100M of stock in Q3 2026.

chapters.title: Why it's on the radar: the 13F view
chapters.lede: TGTX made the Insights tab because 8 of the tracked funds hold it, four as conviction positions, and it has the strongest six-month return of the three stock picks.

blocks.html: Big buyers in Q2 2026: D. E. Shaw lifted its stake to about $187M and Two Sigma to about $136M, each roughly tripling in value. Bridgewater holds it at about 0.10% of its book, one of its larger healthcare weights in this dataset.

chapters.title: Future outlook: opportunities & risks
chapters.lede: Analysts are split more sharply on TG than on the other picks. Targets range from $20 to $86, and the stock trades above the consensus. The key questions are how long Briumvi can keep gaining share and whether the subcutaneous trial succeeds.

blocks.note: Benzinga's consensus was about $51.45 as of Oct 22, 2026, and Google Finance's 3-month average was about $59.43. Walnut's July 2026 count was 7 Buy, 0 Hold and 1 Sell. Targets were set on different dates in 2026.

opp: A successful Phase 3 would close the format gap with Kesimpta and Ocrevus and could support quarterly at-home dosing from 2028.
Growth of 50%+ shows Briumvi is still taking patients, both new starts and switches.
A self-funding business can return cash. TG bought back about $100M in Q3.
The European partnership adds revenue without TG building its own sales force there.
Myasthenia gravis, schizophrenia and azer-cel could each add a second leg.
A profitable, growing neurology franchise could interest larger drug makers.
risk: Almost all revenue comes from one drug in one country.
Kesimpta's self-injection and subcutaneous Ocrevus target patients who prefer to avoid infusions.
Eventual Ocrevus biosimilars and Medicare price negotiation could compress prices across the class.
A subcutaneous Phase 3 miss would hurt the long-term story.
Growth fell from 64% to 52% in a quarter, and the rate of slowdown drives the valuation.
The stock trades above the consensus target, and BofA's $20 target implies about 70% downside.

items: Briumvi growth fades as the subcutaneous rivals and later biosimilars arrive. The subcutaneous trial disappoints and the pipeline is too early to fill the gap.
Briumvi is a good franchise, but the price already assumes a lot. Fair value is closer to $50 until the subcutaneous data are in.
US sales pass $1B in 2027, buybacks continue, and the subcutaneous trial succeeds, but the competition limits the multiple.
Subcutaneous success plus share gains drive several more years of double-digit growth and strong margins.
Briumvi becomes the anti-CD20 of choice in both formats, a pipeline program works, and TG becomes a takeover target.
The biggest binary event: success defends the franchise against home-dosing rivals.
This sets growth expectations for Briumvi's fifth year.
Phase 2 data: myasthenia gravis, schizophrenia, azer-cel
The first evidence of a second product.
The pace of repurchases signals management's confidence.

glossary: An autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the protective coating of nerves, causing relapses and disability.
Forms of MS with distinct attacks followed by partial or full recovery. Briumvi is approved for these.
An autoimmune disease that causes muscle weakness. TG is testing B-cell therapy in it.
Chronic lymphocytic leukemia, the blood cancer TG's first program targeted.
An immune cell that makes antibodies. B cells are thought to drive MS attacks.
An antibody that targets CD20 on B cells and depletes them. Briumvi, Ocrevus and Kesimpta all work this way.
The anti-CD20 antibody sold as Briumvi.
TG's oral PI3K-delta inhibitor for lymphoma. It was withdrawn in 2022.
A class of cancer pills that block a signaling enzyme. The FDA tightened its scrutiny of the class in 2022.
Immune cells engineered to attack a target. Azer-cel is TG's version for autoimmune disease.
Given as an injection under the skin, often at home, instead of an IV infusion.
How a drug is absorbed and cleared. PK modeling supports TG's quarterly subcutaneous dosing plan.
TG's anti-CD20 MS drug. It is given as a one-hour infusion twice a year after the first doses.
Roche's anti-CD20 MS drug (ocrelizumab), the category leader.
Novartis's anti-CD20 MS drug (ofatumumab), a monthly self-injection.
An oral drug class in MS development. Analysts see it competing mostly with other pills rather than with anti-CD20 drugs.
A near-copy of a biologic drug that arrives after the original's exclusivity ends.
The US Food and Drug Administration, which approves drugs.
An early FDA approval based on surrogate data. It can be withdrawn if confirmatory trials fail, as happened with Ukoniq.
Biologics License Application: the filing that asks the FDA to approve a biologic drug.
The FDA's target date for deciding on an application.
Mid-stage and late-stage trials. Phase 3 results support an approval filing.
The first headline results of a trial, before the full data set.
How long patients live. Concerns about it led to Ukoniq's withdrawal.
A trial that compares a drug with an existing treatment rather than a placebo. ULTIMATE compared ublituximab with teriflunomide.
Sales after discounts, rebates and returns.
A company buying its own shares, which reduces the share count.
An analyst's estimate of where the stock will trade in about 12 months.
